newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London lower in quiet trade.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London edged lower in quiet trade on Tuesday, with some interest in blue-chips in a market where interest has been oscillating between exporting and bank issues, traders said.

The Nikkei 50 index of leading shares traded in London was up 9.42 points, or 0.65 percent, from London's Monday close at 1,454.56 by 1345 GMT, marking a retreat from Tokyo where the Nikkei 225 ended 173.08 points or 0.92 percent firmer at 19,070.07.
"It's been very quiet," one trader said, "We've seen some buying interest in exporters, but it's just been scraps."
There was some selling in Toyota, down 15 yen at 3,190 yen, he added. "It looks like there's a switch out of Toyota into Nissan." Nissan was some 2.5 yen firmer at 753 yen.
"Bank issues are generally quiet at the moment," he added. "The market is in rotation. Blue chip exporters are popular one day, bank issues the next. The rest of the market is being ignored really."
